start.text:
The cart of the shop counted money in floating point: its total drifted from the receipt by a cent, and a coupon could take it below zero.
The Epic moves prices to whole cents, the cart total and the discount onto them.

steps.text:
The cart added prices as floating-point numbers, so three items at 0.10 came to 0.30000000000000004 and the
receipt showed 0.29 after rounding down. Lines with a quantity of zero were still counted.

steps.title: The total is a sum of whole cents
steps.whatItDoes: turns each price into whole cents first and only then multiplies and adds, so no fraction of a cent is ever stored; a line with a zero or negative quantity is skipped.
steps.whyHere: the total is the one place every later sum starts from — the coupon and the receipt read it.
steps.risks: a price with three decimals ("0.105") throws in `toCents`; no test feeds one.

steps.title: Checkout needs a positive quantity
steps.whatItDoes: lets the cart go to checkout only when at least one line would be charged.
steps.whyHere: the same rule as the skip in `cartTotal`; keeping both in one file keeps them in step.
steps.withoutIt: a cart of zero-quantity lines would reach checkout with a total of 0.

steps.text:
The receipt still formats the total with `formatCents`; its rounding was right and the ticket did not ask to touch
it.
`pnpm test test/unit/cart.test.ts` exit 0: three items at 0.10 make 30 cents; a zero-quantity line adds nothing.
